ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, representatives, ultimate beneficial owners, and proposed SAS officers against: (i) United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) EU Council implementing regulations (EU CFSP sanctions, including Russia/Belarus/other restrictive measures); (iii) French domestic sanctions and restrictive measures issued by the Direction Générale du Trésor; (iv) national Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) database derived from official public functions registers; and (v) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list to the extent the subscription box commercial flows may touch USD or U.S. correspondent banking. In addition, enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any individual or company resident in or controlled from a FATF high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdiction; suspicious transactions or identity mismatches must be reported to TRACFIN under Article L561-15 of the Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (INPI) — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; pre-clearance search also via INPI's Open Data and Infogreffe (greffe du tribunal de commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company's chosen name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin script and be registered in French-language statutory documentation; foreign-script names must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must not be misleading, must comply with the SAS required suffix 'Société par actions simplifiée' or 'SAS', must not infringe prior trademarks or trade names, and must not improperly evoke public entities, sovereign emblems, French Republic, or regulated professions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the INPI (administered via the Guichet Unique), the applicant may file a 'recours gracieux' (administrative appeal) with the INPI within two months of the notification, providing a legal argument or withdrawal of conflicting prior rights. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful or remains unanswered for the statutory period, a 'recours contentieux' may be lodged before the Administrative Court (Tribunal administratif de Paris) within two months of the rejection decision. Where the rejection derives from a prior trademark right, the applicant may request a written consent/withdrawal from the prior right holder and resubmit. In the absence of a response within the applicable regulatory silence period (5 business days for a complete filing), the name application is deemed accepted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible through a professional commercial domiciliation provider (domiciliation d'entreprise), which supplies a physical registered office address, mail reception, and legal service access. This model is common for subscription-box e-commerce and does not in itself trigger adverse tax treatment, provided the actual economic substance (warehousing, fulfilment, decision-making) is carried on at a separate defined location. If the SAS operates as a pure e-commerce reseller without physical local inventory, the registered office may constitute a 'centres minor de décision' for tax residence purposes. Registration with the police prefecture as a domiciliation is optional but recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate quantified risk: 30–35% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the French tax administration (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques) or the URSSAF (social security collection agency) within the first three operating years, with the risk significantly increasing if the company declares a commercial warehouse, uses reverse-charge VAT on imports, or has a high ratio of reported online sales revenues.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); official portal: www.impots.gouv.fr; corporate registration via the Guichet Unique (procedure.gouv.fr) administered in coordination with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident founder forms the SAS by drafting and filing articles of incorporation through the Guichet Unique, obtaining a SIREN/SIRET from INSEE; the competent SIE then allocates the corporate tax account reference (numéro de gestion) and issues the intra-Community VAT identification number (TVA intracommunautaire) following the Article 286-ter CGI registration filing. A foreign entity not incorporated in France but carrying on taxable French activities must apply for French VAT registration using the simplified non-resident application (form n°3559 / MO/CA) with the Non-Resident SIE of Joinville-le-Pont; a fiscal representative under Article 289-A CGI is mandatory for non-EU tax-resident operators unless a European scheme exception applies. Newly incorporated SAS entities must also transmit a tax-status attestation to the DGFiP within 15 days of registration per Article 302 septies-A CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not maintain a general check-the-box entity classification regime; an SAS is mandatorily taxed at entity level under Impôt sur les Sociétés. Available statutory elections include: (i) fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223-A CGI, enabling an SAS group head holding at least 95% of French subsidiaries to consolidate their results into a single corporate income tax return; (ii) election for centralised group VAT registration and filing; (iii) option to apply the monthly normal VAT settlement regime in lieu of the automatic simplified regime; (iv) hybrid mismatch provisions (Articles 212-II and 212-IX CGI, implementing the ATAD) provide no elective classification but impose a documentary justification obligation to avoid deduction disallowance where a payment has not been taxed or deducted in the counterparty jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a taxable person established in France, VAT liability arises on the first taxable transaction, subject to the franchise en base exemption at an annual goods turnover below €85,800 (Article 293-B CGI; threshold indexed by decree; services threshold: €37,500). Above these ceilings, VAT registration is mandatory. For intra-EU distance sales of subscription boxes to consumers in other Member States, registration is due in the destination State once the annual cross-border turnover exceeds €10,000, unless the operator opts to register the OSS; a non-established foreign seller has no de minimis threshold and must register from the first taxable supply located in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates a phasing-in electronic invoicing regime: from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons must be able to receive structured e-invoices, large and mid-size enterprises must issue via a certified Dématérialisation Partner (PDP) or the public Invoice Platform (PPF), and from 1 September 2027 all small businesses must also issue e-invoices. There is no per-invoice digital stamping or real-time fiscal clearance; instead, the requirement is structured transmission of invoice lifecycle events and monthly e-reporting of B2C and international transaction data through secured APIs to the PPF. Failure to transmit exposes the supplier to fines of up to €15,000 per obligation under Articles 173 and 1737 CGI, plus loss of input VAT deduction where the invoice does not satisfy Articles 289 requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical export of subscription-box goods to non-EU destinations qualifies for the 0% French VAT rate under Article 262-I-1° CGI, provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory and the exporter or its customs agent holds a valid export declaration (DAU/MRN). Deliveries to EU B2B customers are zero-rated under Article 258-A CGI only when the customer's EU VAT number is validated and transport to the destination Member State is evidenced. Exports to the French overseas territories and départements d'outre-mer, which lie outside the EU VAT customs territory, may also be exempted on the same evidence basis. The burden of proof rests entirely on the subscription-box operator, and the DGFiP together with the Customs Authority (DGDDI) require a complete documentary chain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique / DAU) bearing the MRN
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing international carriage outside the EU
Transport contract and carrier booking confirmation showing dispatch from France
Proof of third-country customs entry or verified offloading at destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing settlement of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are audited through the French statutory verification procedure (vérification de comptabilité) with a standard three-year reassessment period (Articles L. 169 and L. 176 LPF), extended to six years in cases of concealed activity. If zero-rating is disallowed, the DGFiP reassesses French VAT at 20% plus monthly late interest of 0.20% (Article 1727 CGI) and penalty of 10% for late declaration, 40% for deliberate under-declaration (Article 1729-a), and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (Article 1729-b); defective invoice documentation can additionally trigger fines of up to €15,000 per document under Article 1737 CGI and loss of input VAT deduction. Where customs fraud is established, Article 414 of the French Customs Code provides fines of one to three times the evaded VAT and imprisonment of up to three years, and the clawback may be reinforced by a supplementary assessment period of up to ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR). The foreign-exchange administration function is exercised by the Direction Générale du Trésor at the French Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Sovereign, Industry and Digital Sovereignty, subject to European Union treaty obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies the EU free movement of capital under Article 63 TFEU; the euro is fully convertible for current and capital transactions. No prior exchange-control authorization is required for ordinary cross-border payments in and out of France, except for measures imposed by EU sanctions, counter-terrorist financing, and anti-money-laundering legislation. Current account convertibility is unfettered: trade, service, royalties, and payment-card settlement flows can circulate freely. Capital account convertibility is likewise unrestricted, but a French resident company must report material cross-border capital, loan, and foreign-exchange transactions to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. Profit remittance hurdles for a French SAS are procedural rather than FX-related: distributable profits must satisfy legal-reserve and dividend-payment requirements under the French Commercial Code; a dividend paid to a non-resident shareholder may attract French withholding tax unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; and the paying bank may require the shareholder's tax-residence certificate or an IFU form before releasing the remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose mandatory surrender or mandatory conversion of foreign-currency export proceeds into euro. A French SAS may retain export receipts in a foreign-currency account, or 'compte en devises', at a French or EEA credit institution. There is no statutory 30-day surrender timeline and no minimum conversion ratio. French exchange control only requires commercial documentation and Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting when cross-border transactions reach applicable reporting thresholds. The company should ensure that export invoices, customs declarations, and bank settlement records are complete and consistent, and that the account is designated as foreign-currency-denominated if such receipts are expected.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. (LCL / Groupe Crédit Agricole)
Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale (Crédit Mutuel and CIC)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall feasibility for a French SAS: Medium. An ACPR-regulated electronic-money institution or payment institution such as Qonto or Finom can be useful for day-to-day EUR collections, Stripe payout reception, and SEPA payments. However, such EMIs are not full credit institutions and cannot provide capital-escrow services, commercial credit, documentary letters of credit, margin-based FX derivatives, or full cross-border treasury clearing. Offshore EMIs domiciled outside France/EEA are generally not viable as primary treasury or escrow accounts because they lack the PSD2 'single passport' and are not recognized as eligible receiving institutions by French banks for capital-deposit certificates. An EU-licensed EMI with a valid passport may hold segregated client funds, but it cannot be a substitute for a supervised French credit institution when the SAS requires trade finance, FX hedging, or correspondent-banking liquidity infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/KYC under Articles L.561-5 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code permits non-face-to-face onboarding only where strong identity-verification technology is used, such as an ACPR-validated eIDAS qualified electronic signature or secure video identification. In practice, most first-line French banks require at least one physical visit by the legal representative, normally the President of the SAS, or by a France-resident representative holding a notarized power of attorney; the directors are not required to appear collectively. Remote onboarding is accepted by certain fintech and online banks, but those accounts are not suitable for blocked share-capital escrows or large commercial-letter-of-credit operations. The standard requirement is a certified copy of a passport or national identity card, proof of residence, corporate KYC pack, and an interview verifying the purpose and economic substance of the cross-border subscription-box business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain involving an offshore shareholder or layered corporate structure that delays identification of the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filed with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; complete share-register chronology; registered-office certificates at every entity level; notarized and apostilled passports or identity cards of all natural-person UBOs; sworn translations of foreign company extracts; bank reference letters; and a written organigram showing each legal entity and ownership percentage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident president or legal representative without EU residence, flagged for enhanced due diligence and uncertainty on signatory authority.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport or national identity card with apostille or certified true-copy certification; proof of fiscal residency; certificate of good standing from the foreign registry; corporate resolution appointing the president; notarized French power of attorney delegating authority to an in-country representative; professional references; and source-of-funds statement for any capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border e-commerce merchant with recurring subscription payments, refunds, and chargebacks, perceived as a potential AB/CF risk despite low nominal AML risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant agreements with Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net; payout and settlement transaction history; customer terms and conditions with AML-compliant refund and chargeback policies; anti-fraud and sanctions-screening procedures; GDPR privacy documentation; audited or management financial statements; cash-flow forecast; and a clear map of supplier and logistics relationships proving physical-goods deliveries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring subscription commerce typology in which transactions are not supported by discrete one-off invoices, making transaction-purpose verification difficult.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed subscription-box business plan; public website and pricing page; complete terms of sale; sample customer invoices and order confirmations; VAT registration certificate and EORI number; product descriptions and ISIC-compatible trade codes; supplier purchase orders and delivery notes; and a bank-policy-compliant transaction-monitoring response demonstrating that each recurring payment corresponds to a contractual subscription installment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions into the French SAS should be routed via SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR from an EEA shareholder, or via SWIFT MT103 in non-EUR from a non-EEA shareholder. The payment instruction must identify the beneficiary by legal name, French IBAN, SIREN/RCS registration number, and must state the purpose as 'Souscription au capital social / augmentation de capital' rather than a generic remittance. The bank-specific SWIFT/OECD balance-of-payments purpose code for equity capital contribution must be used, together with the subscription deed and, where funds are deposited before RCS registration, a bank certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds). The supporting verification file must include the shareholders' meeting minutes or sole-shareholder decision, printed subscription form, proof of bank funds deposit, updated bylaws, and the RCS/Kbis extract showing the registered capital increase.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring subscription-box merchandise imports, the preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct post-shipment cross-border supplier payments; for EUR suppliers inside SEPA, a standard SEPA Credit Transfer is sufficient. For higher-value bulk orders with open-account risk, the French SAS may use an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (commercial LC) opened by its French bank and transmitted by MT700/MT707, with the seller presenting compliant transport and invoice documents. Documentary collections with drafts on an approval basis are also available. All outbound payments must reference the supplier invoice number, purchase order, Incoterms 2020 rule, customs/EORI numbers, and the relevant commodity description for ISIC 4791 subscription-box merchandise. If a foreign-currency payment is required, settlement must clear through the same bank's correspondent network using MT103 or MT202 COV with appropriate purpose codes, ensuring the French company's FX hedging and treasury instruction matches the underlying trade document.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign-exchange transactions for immediate trade settlement where a commercial invoice or payment instruction exists.
Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts (achats/ventes à terme de devises) covering confirmed trade payables or receivables.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies that lack a fully convertible or deliverable offshore market, provided the underlying commercial exposure is documented.
FX swaps for matched cash-flow liquidity management, including conversion of export proceeds and future trade payables.
Cross-currency swaps for long-term financing structures involving external loans, intercompany financing, or treasury netting where permitted by the bank and MiFID eligibility.
European-style currency options and zero-premium collars used strictly to hedge transactional currency risk, never as speculative open positions under French banking and markets regulation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability, possible judicial injunction, and penalties for failure to approve accounts; no automatic fixed-time strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts and required corporate reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the Commercial Court through the French business one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial injunction and civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance; prolonged inactivity or unresolved non-compliance may support registry removal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; electronic filing is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and generally a 10% surcharge, increasing for formal notice or aggravated non-compliance; tax collection enforcement may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December each year through the business tax account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge and interest; no direct administrative strike-off mechanism.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of the Commercial Court through the French business one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing; update within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership or related information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice, court-ordered compliance, criminal penalties for inaccurate or omitted information, and potential registry-related restrictions; no automatic annual strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million pre-tax turnover, or 50 average employees. Additional audit obligations may arise for qualifying parent, subsidiary, or group structures.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations; IFRS may apply voluntarily or to qualifying consolidated accounts where legally permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual UBO confirmation for an SAS. The company must maintain accurate information and file an amendment within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership, control, or declarable particulars.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share transfers
Register of decisions of the shareholders or sole shareholder
Register of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,625-5,400 for a small SAS, depending on transaction volume, group structure, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 5% of eligible R&D expenses), innovation status benefits, regional investment tax incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1201 - Déclaration de résultat, filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr or B2B portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15th day of the 4th month following fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 April for 31 December year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for French tax residents filing on worldwide income; non-residents report only French-source income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for residents; non-residents include only French-source profits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay (minimum €125, maximum 10% of tax due); possible criminal sanctions for fraudulent filings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for domestic distributions to French residents; 12.8% for non-resident recipients (reduced under applicable double tax treaties)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate from foreign authority and submit withholding tax relief application form via impots.gouv.fr portal
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory rate (reduced to 0-10% under most treaties); Interest: 10% statutory rate (reduced to 0% under many treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: General economic substance requirements under OECD BEPS framework and French anti-abuse rules for tax residency and compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false statements in tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 80% of evaded tax, imprisonment up to 5 years, and repayment of evaded taxes with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, fines, and disqualification from corporate offices

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a company without real economic activity or substance for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as disregarded entity, back taxation, penalties up to 80% of additional tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for fraudulent management, fines, and possible imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of non-arm's length prices without supporting documentation or failure to file TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, penalties of 80% of additional tax due, and interest charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability if directors knowingly approved non-compliant arrangements

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform KYC, conduct due diligence, or report suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 5% of annual turnover, criminal penalties, asset freezes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and imprisonment for willful non-compliance
